name: CL01 rows: feed's whole-run clock reads 0
why: a stuck clock: the ONE-line row (ratio false, decided by totalMs alone) passes on the old whole-buffer logic with it; the helper row only asserts 0 <= totalMs < 1000 (finding C03, TD-1(b))

name: CL02 rows: feed's whole-run clock is the first tenth only
why: the ONE-line 16 MiB row passes the old logic's 13 s of work with it (finding TD-1(b), variant (c))

name: CL03 rows: feed's first-tenth clock reads 0
why: the ratio then compares the last tenth with nothing but the 100 ms floor; no row asserts the first-tenth number

name: CL04 rows: feed's last-tenth clock reads 0
why: the ratio is then always met, so a quadratic scanner is judged by the whole-run limit alone

name: CL05 rows: feed's last-tenth clock is the whole run
why: the last-tenth number then contains the first nine tenths; no row asserts it

name: CL06 rows: feed's windows are a fifth of the pushes
why: the first and last windows are twice as long as their name says; no row asserts the window size

name: CL07 rows: feed's clock stops where it started
why: the whole-run and last-tenth numbers are zero or negative; the helper row accepts totalMs of 0

name: LL01 push: the kept tail is capped to its last 65,536 characters (after 16 pieces)
why: a marker line longer than 64 KiB loses its start; no row has a Browse at line that long (the 100,000-character line holds only x, the seeded lines are at most 400 characters) (finding M-R43, TD-3)

name: LL02 push: the kept tail is capped to its last 4,096 characters (checked every 1,024 pieces)
why: the same family with a small cap that only one-byte chunks reach (finding TD-3)

name: LL03 push: the kept tail is capped to its last 65,536 characters (after 64 pieces)
why: the reviewer's first variant (finding TD-3)

name: LL04 push: the kept tail is capped to its FIRST 65,536 characters
why: a long line of noise that ENDS in the marker loses the marker; no row has a line like that

name: LL05 push: the kept tail is capped to its last 1 MiB (checked every 16 pieces)
why: a cap above every line the rows send; only a marker line of more than 1 MiB loses its start

name: LL06 push: the completed text is capped to its last 65,536 characters
why: the lines being tested are cut to their end; a marker whose start is more than 64 KiB before its newline is never seen

name: SP01 push: the new text's whole escapes are stripped before the join
why: a whole escape spliced into a cut one (ESC [ 0, a whole escape, m) is stripped here and then again by parseBrowseUrl; no generator makes one (finding M-R44-R45)

name: SP02 push: the kept tail's whole escapes are stripped when it is kept
why: the same family on the other side of the join (finding M-R44-R45)

name: EA01 push: the unfinished line is read as if its newline had arrived (answers early)
why: answers at the push that brings the last character of the URL, before its newline; the row 'answers null at every push before the first answer, for every case' cannot see it (its slice ends at the first non-null answer by definition); run with -t on that row alone, it SURVIVES (finding TD-6)

name: WI01 adapter: a dead stub scanner, the real call in a trailing comment, the factory kept alive by `void`
to:
const urlScanner = { push: (_text: string): string | null => null }; // const urlScanner = createBrowseUrlScanner();
      void createBrowseUrlScanner;
why: the preview would never find its URL; the comment stripper leaves a TRAILING comment, so the spelling is still in the text (finding TD-4, V1)

name: WI02 adapter: an accumulator under another name
why: the whole stderr is accumulated again; the gate looks for the identifier stderr, not for the accumulation (finding TD-4, V2)

name: WI03 adapter: a harmless trailing comment that names parseBrowseUrl
to: let urlShown = false; // formerly fed to parseBrowseUrl
why: EQUIVALENT: a comment is not code and changes nothing; the gate must not refuse it, and today it does (it strips whole-line comments only), so this verdict is a false kill (finding TD-4, V3)

name: WI04 adapter: stdout chunks are fed to the scanner too
why: the scanner's partial line would take stdout bytes (stderr x/ and stdout noise give xnoise/); the pin reads only the stderr handler's slice (finding M-R58)

name: WI05 adapter: showPreview gets the chunk and not the URL
why: the pin ends at `urlShown=true;`, so what follows in the handler is unpinned; only the integration preview test would see it (finding M-R59)

name: WI06 adapter: the stderr is accumulated into a property, as the handler's first statement
why: a `+=` on a string that is not a local, before the statements the contiguous pin reads; the gate pins the identifier stderr only (an insert AFTER `const text` breaks that pin's contiguity and is killed, as the first draft of this mutant was)
